What the app can do and how to set it up

Shows the current weather in the iGO navigator through a compatible skin: Primo, NextGen, Pioneer AVIC and other builds.

• The service finds where you are, gets the weather from Open-Meteo (free, no sign-up) and writes it into the iGO profile.
• If the skin passes the coordinates of the route destination, the weather there is written too.
• The main screen shows temperature, humidity, pressure and wind; the background and picture follow the weather.
• While the service runs, a notification with the weather stays in the shade: without it Android 8 and newer stops background services.

1. Open Settings → iGO folder and choose the navigator folder — the one that holds save.
2. Optionally turn on Launch iGO and choose the Navigator package.
3. Tap Start service and allow access to the location and notifications.
4. In a few seconds the weather appears on the main screen and in the skin.

You need internet and a skin that shows the weather from weather.txt.
The iGO folder and the folder picker

Usually the folder is chosen in the Android system picker: find the folder with save, tap “Use this folder” and allow access. If the memory card is not shown, turn it on in the picker’s “⋮” menu.

Many head units have no system picker. Whether yours has one is shown in Settings → System folder picker, right below the iGO folder.
• Android 10 and older: the app asks for storage access, finds iGO folders on the internal storage, memory cards and USB drives and lists them. If the folder is not listed, choose “Enter the path…” and type it, for example /storage/sdcard1/iGO.
• Android 11 and newer without the system picker cannot choose a folder at all: this is a limit of the firmware.

• Turn on Launch iGO and choose the navigator package: iGO starts with the service and the app closes.
• The second icon “Weather service” starts the service and the navigator with one tap. It can replace the usual iGO icon.
• If something is not set up yet, the icon opens the main screen.

• Units: metric (°C, m/s) or imperial (°F, mph).
• Update period: from 10 minutes to 3 hours. To update now, use the button in the toolbar or pull down.
• Write to all profiles: profiles 01–04, not only 01.
• Sound after every update and stopping the service when the screen turns off.
• Animations: turn them off if the head unit feels slow.

All files are in save/profiles/NN/userlists/, UTF-16 encoded.

• weather.txt — written by the service: temperature;icon.svg;description;id, e.g. -3°C;13n.svg;Snow;601.
• coordinates_fin.txt — written by the skin: latitude;longitude, 0;0 — no route.
• weather_fin.txt — written by the service: temperature;icon.svg;place.

Icons and codes match OpenWeatherMap, so skins made for 1.x keep working. When the service stops, the weather files are cleared.

• “No permission to write to the iGO folder” — choose the folder again in the settings.
• “The iGO folder has no …” — wrong folder: choose the one that holds save.
• “Waiting for coordinates…” — turn on the location and check that the app may use it.
• “No internet” — the service tries again later by itself.
• Weather in the app but not in the skin — check that the skin shows weather and uses the same profile.
• The folder cannot be chosen — look at “System folder picker” in the settings.

Weather data: Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0.
